parts.zh: W: 欢迎收听《金钱 matters》
W: 钱有一种魔力。如果事先不做规划
M: 嗯，关键就是要记录你的资金收支
W: 说起来容易做起来难
M: 是的，但了解自己的收入和支出
W: 我总是惊讶于自己的开支加起来竟然那么多
M: 没错，大多数人根本不知道自己每天花了多少钱
M: 嗯，这还不至于造成灾难

items.stem: What does the man say about the weekly program?

choices.text: It enables people to earn more money.
choices.zh: 它能让人们赚更多钱。

choices.text: It teaches the importance of financing.
choices.zh: 它教授理财的重要性。

choices.text: It helps people with budgeting.
choices.zh: 它帮助人们做预算。

choices.text: It introduces a novel way to invest.
choices.zh: 它介绍了一种新颖的投资方式。

items.stem: What did the man read recently?

choices.text: Many Americans are not satisfied with their income.
choices.zh: 许多美国人对自己的收入不满意。

choices.text: Many Americans have no idea about how to invest.
choices.zh: 许多美国人不知道如何投资。

choices.text: Most Americans do not know how to save money.
choices.zh: 大多数美国人不知道如何省钱。

choices.text: Most Americans do not stick to a budget.
choices.zh: 大多数美国人不坚持预算。

items.stem: What does the woman suggest the man do first to avoid getting into debt?

choices.text: Keep track of his money.
choices.zh: 记录他的钱款。

choices.text: Live within his means.
choices.zh: 量入为出。

choices.text: Find more sources of income.
choices.zh: 寻找更多收入来源。

choices.text: Refrain from buying luxuries.
choices.zh: 克制购买奢侈品。

items.stem: What does the woman say about online shopping?

choices.text: It offers a greater variety of items.
choices.zh: 它提供更多种类的商品。

choices.text: It helps avoid unnecessary spending.
choices.zh: 它有助于避免不必要的开支。

choices.text: It changes one's way of living.
choices.zh: 它改变人们的生活方式。

choices.text: It saves one's time for shopping.
choices.zh: 它节省购物时间。

items.stem: What does the woman say about the flat?

choices.text: It is brand-new.
choices.zh: 它是全新的。

choices.text: It has plenty of rooms.
choices.zh: 它有很多房间。

choices.text: It belongs to her mother.
choices.zh: 它属于她母亲。

choices.text: It has been vacant for months.
choices.zh: 它已经空置好几个月了。

items.stem: What is the man's chief consideration in looking for a flat?

choices.text: Space.
choices.zh: 空间。

choices.text: Tranquillity.
choices.zh: 安静。

choices.text: Appliances.
choices.zh: 家用电器。

choices.text: Location.
choices.zh: 位置。

items.stem: What does the man have to do on signing the contract?

choices.text: Talk to his wife about the contract terms.
choices.zh: 和妻子谈谈合同条款。

choices.text: Pay the first month's rent and a deposit.
choices.zh: 支付第一个月的租金和押金。

choices.text: Check the references of the flat owner.
choices.zh: 核查公寓房东的资信证明。

choices.text: Consult his solicitor one more time.
choices.zh: 再咨询一次他的律师。

items.stem: Why does the man say his wife will feel very excited if they move into the flat?

choices.text: She can have a wonderful view of the pond.
choices.zh: 她可以欣赏到池塘的美妙景色。

choices.text: She will be much closer to her work place.
choices.zh: 她离工作地点会近得多。

choices.text: She can make friends with new neighbours.
choices.zh: 她可以和新邻居交朋友。

choices.text: She will have plenty of space for her shoes.
choices.zh: 她将有足够的空间放她的鞋子。

items.stem: What has the new study found about children watching television?

choices.text: The more commercials they see, the more brands they get to know.
choices.zh: 他们看的广告越多，了解的品牌就越多。

choices.text: The more commercials they see, the more they adore celebrities.
choices.zh: 他们看的广告越多，就越崇拜名人。

choices.text: The more television they watch, the fewer conflicts in the family.
choices.zh: 他们看的电视越多，家庭冲突就越少。

choices.text: The more television they watch, the greater their parents' stress.
choices.zh: 他们看的电视越多，父母的压力就越大。

items.stem: What are parents advised to do to reduce the impact of TV commercials?

choices.text: Inform children of the family's financial situation.
choices.zh: 告知孩子家庭的财务状况。

choices.text: Shift children's attention to interesting activities.
choices.zh: 将孩子的注意力转移到有趣的活动上。

choices.text: Involve children in making purchasing decisions.
choices.zh: 让孩子参与购买决策。

choices.text: Help children understand advertising's intent.
choices.zh: 帮助孩子理解广告的意图。

items.stem: What makes children particularly vulnerable to TV commercials?

choices.text: Their limited cognitive ability.
choices.zh: 他们有限的认知能力。

choices.text: Their strong natural curiosity.
choices.zh: 他们强烈的天生好奇心。

choices.text: Their admiration for celebrities.
choices.zh: 他们对名人的崇拜。

choices.text: Their lack of social experience.
choices.zh: 他们缺乏社会经验。

items.stem: What baffling phenomenon is discussed in the passage?

choices.text: Bad guys may do good deeds.
choices.zh: 坏人可能做好事。

choices.text: Bad guys may go unpunished.
choices.zh: 坏人可能逃脱惩罚。

choices.text: Good guys may not always cooperate.
choices.zh: 好人可能并不总是合作。

choices.text: Good guys may get unfair treatment.
choices.zh: 好人可能受到不公平对待。

items.stem: How are we all judged according to the passage?

choices.text: By what we do.
choices.zh: 通过我们所做的事。

choices.text: By fair evaluation.
choices.zh: 通过公正的评价。

choices.text: In comparison with others.
choices.zh: 通过与他人比较。

choices.text: In accordance with set standards.
choices.zh: 根据既定标准。

items.stem: What can a normal person do when faced with people who perform better?

choices.text: Learn from them earnestly.
choices.zh: 认真向他们学习。

choices.text: Compete with them actively.
choices.zh: 积极与他们竞争。

choices.text: Leave them alone temporarily.
choices.zh: 暂时不理会他们。

choices.text: Cooperate with them sincerely.
choices.zh: 真诚地与他们合作。

items.stem: What may discourage people from performing good deeds?

choices.text: Being dismissed as hypocritical.
choices.zh: 被当作虚伪而遭到否定。

choices.text: Not getting the reward they deserve.
choices.zh: 得不到应得的回报。

choices.text: Having to make too many sacrifices.
choices.zh: 不得不做出太多牺牲。

choices.text: Being misunderstood by people around.
choices.zh: 被周围的人误解。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about most preteen children?

choices.text: They are increasingly aware of gender differences.
choices.zh: 他们越来越意识到性别差异。

choices.text: They engage themselves in positive recollection.
choices.zh: 他们进行积极的回忆。

choices.text: They begin to see the importance of friendship.
choices.zh: 他们开始认识到友谊的重要性。

choices.text: They make friends with peers of the same sex.
choices.zh: 他们与同性同龄人交朋友。

items.stem: What do most males devote much of their energy to during adolescence?

choices.text: Competing for position.
choices.zh: 争夺地位。

choices.text: Forging close ties with friends.
choices.zh: 与朋友建立亲密关系。

choices.text: Pursuing fashion.
choices.zh: 追求时尚。

choices.text: Fulfilling family obligations.
choices.zh: 履行家庭义务。

items.stem: What do children do when they reach late adolescence?

choices.text: They prioritize romance over friendship.
choices.zh: 他们把恋爱置于友谊之上。

choices.text: They try to strengthen same-sex friendships.
choices.zh: 他们试图加强同性友谊。

choices.text: They begin to take friendship more seriously.
choices.zh: 他们开始更认真地对待友谊。

choices.text: They compete intensely for romantic partners.
choices.zh: 他们为争夺恋爱对象而激烈竞争。

items.stem: Why do disabled job applicants feel reluctant to disclose their disability information?

choices.text: They regard it as a matter of sheer privacy.
choices.zh: 他们认为这纯粹是隐私问题。

choices.text: They are worried about being turned down.
choices.zh: 他们担心会被拒绝。

choices.text: They fear that their condition will be made widely known.
choices.zh: 他们害怕自己的状况会被广泛知晓。

choices.text: They are afraid to be discriminated against once recruited.
choices.zh: 他们害怕一旦被录用就会受到歧视。

items.stem: When does the speaker suggest applicants reveal their disability information?

choices.text: After receiving a job offer.
choices.zh: 在收到工作邀约之后。

choices.text: During a job interview.
choices.zh: 在工作面试期间。

choices.text: When confirming an interview.
choices.zh: 在确认面试时。

choices.text: Upon completing a cover letter.
choices.zh: 在完成求职信时。

items.stem: What are people advised to do when filling out their job application form?

choices.text: Describe the true state of their health.
choices.zh: 描述他们健康状况的真实情况。

choices.text: Provide all the information required.
choices.zh: 提供所有要求的信息。

choices.text: Stress the irrelevance of their disability to the job.
choices.zh: 强调他们的残障与工作无关。

choices.text: Avoid mentioning the name of their disability.
choices.zh: 避免提及他们残障的名称。

items.stem: What did some American researchers find about students' reading comprehension in the presence of background noise?

choices.text: Their scores were least affected by music with speech.
choices.zh: 他们的分数受带有语音的音乐影响最小。

choices.text: It was the poorest when there was background speech.
choices.zh: 当有背景语音时表现最差。

choices.text: Their scores were most depressed with instrumental music.
choices.zh: 他们的分数在有器乐时下降最多。

choices.text: It was disrupted by the sound of an air conditioner or fan.
choices.zh: 受到空调或风扇声音的干扰。

items.stem: What do we learn from the British researchers about the degree of interference from background noise?

choices.text: It has to do with the type and volume of the background noise.
choices.zh: 与背景噪音的类型和音量有关。

choices.text: It has to do with short-term memory for listening comprehension.
choices.zh: 与听力理解的短期记忆有关。

choices.text: It depends on the overlap in processing different kinds of information.
choices.zh: 取决于处理不同类型信息时的重叠程度。

choices.text: It depends on the participants' ability to concentrate on the task at hand.
choices.zh: 取决于参与者专注于手头任务的能力。

items.stem: What is best for students to do when writing essays according to some research?

choices.text: Keep everything as quiet as possible.
choices.zh: 尽可能保持一切安静。

choices.text: Play nothing but instrumental music.
choices.zh: 只播放器乐。

choices.text: Use vocal material as little as possible.
choices.zh: 尽可能少使用声乐材料。

choices.text: Wear a pair of earphones or headphones.
choices.zh: 戴一副耳塞或耳机。

items.stem: How do people of different personalities react to distractions according to other studies?

choices.text: Sociable people were immune to all distractions.
choices.zh: 善于社交的人对所有干扰都免疫。

choices.text: Shy quiet people were most adversely impacted.
choices.zh: 害羞安静的人受到的不利影响最大。

choices.text: Less outgoing people were more affected by silence.
choices.zh: 不太外向的人更容易受到安静环境的影响。

choices.text: Confident people were unaffected by high-arousal music.
choices.zh: 自信的人不受高兴奋度音乐的影响。
